what: ARMS-r3 section 9 (P6) SPARSE_MARKOV decision: the s9 rule and ARMS.md step 6 applied to the counted boots W-1, S-1, W-2, S-2 (W vs S) and S-3, S1024-1, S-4, S1024-2 (S1024 vs S) in results/2026-09-26-serve-r3/. The six earlier boots of the same S config (K-1, K-2, CUR-1, CUR-2, Kp-1, Kp-2) and the S boots of the other pair appear only as labelled robustness context. Computed by decision-markov-compute.py.txt from the raw per-boot files through the readers of decision-bundle-compute.py.txt and the helpers of decision-addons-compute.py.txt; stdlib only.

sources: ARMS-r3 s9: 'Acceptance moves by design, so gate on prose_long c=1 tok/s and L.A.I.L tok/s with the noise rule, and report per boot median_run_acceptance_len and ms/step. Quality quick on one boot per arm.'
ARMS-r3 s9: 'W vs S: revert the default to SPARSE_MARKOV=0 only if W beats S beyond the noise (every W boot beats the S median). Otherwise S stays and S1024 decides.'
ARMS-r3 s9: 'S1024 vs S: promote TOPK=1024 when every S1024 boot beats the S median by more than the noise.'

ARMS.md step 6: primary metric ms/step only at matched acceptance (per-boot median_run_acceptance_len intervals overlap); otherwise 'the arm changed drafting; gate on prose_long c=1 tok/s instead with the same noise rule'. Noise = the larger boot-to-boot spread (max-min of per-boot medians) of the two arms; pass = median improvement > noise AND every B boot beats the A median. Non-inferiority, honest cells, e2e, boot floors, and quality quick before any KEEP.
rule.baselines: W vs S uses S-1, S-2 (the S boots interleaved with W). S1024 vs S uses S-3, S-4 (the S boots interleaved with S1024). ARMS.md: 'the reference is the A boots of the same ABAB sequence'.

readings_recorded.armsmd: median improvement > noise AND every candidate boot beats the base median
readings_recorded.s9_per_boot: every candidate boot beats the base median by more than the noise (used for S1024; stricter)

greedy_output.note: quality_quick selfcons: 12 greedy prompts x 128 tokens, 2 runs per boot. Hazard = first-divergence events / tokens at risk, pooled over every run pair of the named boots (decision-addons-compute.py.txt hazard()). If an arm changed the greedy output, arm-vs-S would diverge more than S-vs-S across boots.

reading: Quality quick passes on every component on all 8 P6 boots (failed_gates empty on each; s9 requires one boot per arm): True.

tools.exact_args: W-1 22/22 []; S-1 21/22 ['t09']; W-2 20/22 ['t01', 't09']; S-2 21/22 ['t09']; S-3 21/22 ['t09']; S1024-1 21/22 ['t09']; S-4 21/22 ['t09']; S1024-2 21/22 ['t09']. 21/22 sits exactly at the 0.9545 limit and 20/22 passes by the gate's one-item slack. The same t09 (and t01) misses show on the 6 earlier K-config boots of the S config (context_tools_exact_failed_K_config_boots), so they are not an arm effect.

Greedy output: W-vs-S and S1024-vs-S cross-arm divergence hazards are at the S-vs-S and all-S-config cross-boot level, consistent with s9's 'greedy verify keeps the output exact, only acceptance moves'.

decision.sparse_markov_verdict: KEEP DSV41_DSPARK_SPARSE_MARKOV=1 (the round-34 default); the revert DSV41_DSPARK_SPARSE_MARKOV=0 is rejected. s9 gate, W minus S tok/s on the counted pair (noise = larger boot-to-boot spread): L.A.I.L W 42.814/43.624 vs S 42.791/42.785, +0.431 against noise 0.81; prose_long c=1 W 44.257/44.196 vs S 44.739/43.336, +0.189 against noise 1.403. Both W boots sit above the S median on both cells, but neither improvement exceeds the noise, so 'W beats S beyond the noise' does not hold and S stays. The trade the task asks about, S relative to W at the same workloads (arm medians): L.A.I.L acceptance -2.74% (-0.0597, noise 0.0421), ms/step -1.48% (-0.735 ms, noise 0.07), tok/s -1%; prose_long c=1 acceptance -1.1% (per-boot intervals overlap, so matched), ms/step -0.603 ms against noise 0.41 with both S boots below the W median, tok/s -0.43%. The acceptance cost roughly cancels the step saving on the two gate cells, and the remaining point difference (W ahead by 1% and 0.43%) is inside the noise. Where acceptance is matched, ARMS.md's primary metric favours S: the prose_long c=1 ms/step reading above, and structured c=1 (acceptance 3.9608 on every boot) -0.576 ms/step (noise 0.284) and +1.003 tok/s (noise 0.5), both beyond the noise.
decision.topk_verdict: PROMOTE DSV41_DSPARK_SPARSE_MARKOV_TOPK=1024 under s9 as written. Counted pair S-3, S1024-1, S-4, S1024-2: L.A.I.L S 42.36/42.871 (median 42.615) vs S1024 43.167/43.615, per-boot margins 0.552/1 against noise 0.511; prose_long c=1 S 42.788/42.195 (median 42.491) vs S1024 44.174/43.728, margins 1.683/1.237 against noise 0.593. Every S1024 boot beats the S median by more than the noise on both gate cells, so both the s9 per-boot reading and the ARMS.md median reading pass. The gain comes through acceptance: prose_long c=1 +0.1062 (+5.15%, noise 0.0214), L.A.I.L +0.0528 (+2.5%, noise 0.0525, so at the noise, not beyond it). The top-1024 gather costs L.A.I.L +0.473 ms/step (noise 0.219); the other c=1 ms/step cells move inside the noise. Four prose c=1, the one primary cell with matched per-boot acceptance, shows no change (+0.184 ms/step against noise 0.384; -0.59 tok/s against 1.63). Non-inferiority holds on every row against the larger spread; the closest is pp_warm_8k (-3.75 against 3.8). Quality quick passes on both S1024 boots, and the greedy S1024-vs-S divergence hazard (0.01691) is at the cross-boot level of the S config itself (S-3 vs S-4 0.016; all 10 S-config boots 0.01924).
caveats: The TOPK pass depends on the pair's own S baseline. Among the 10 S-config boots of this window, S-3 and S-4 rank 2/1 of 10 from the bottom on prose_long c=1 tok/s (42.788/42.195) and 2/1 of 10 on its per-boot acceptance (2.0729/2.0515). Against S-1..S-4 the rule is not met on prose_long c=1 (+0.889 against noise 2.545); L.A.I.L passes the ARMS.md median reading (+0.603 against 0.511) but not the s9 per-boot one (margins 0.379/0.827). Against all 10 S-config boots neither cell meets it (L.A.I.L +0.56 against 1.667; prose_long c=1 +0.26 against 2.699).

Per-boot ranks of the two S1024 boots among 12 (10 S-config + 2 S1024), best first: L.A.I.L acceptance [3, 1] (exact one-sided p 0.0303), L.A.I.L tok/s [4, 1] (p 0.0606), prose_long c=1 acceptance [4, 3] (p 0.1212), prose_long c=1 tok/s [4, 6] (p 0.303). Per run, L.A.I.L acceptance S1024 vs the 10 S-config boots: Hodges-Lehmann +0.0464, p 0.05149. So the L.A.I.L acceptance gain, the mechanism s9 expects (a winner outside the top 1024 is rarer than outside the top 256), holds up across the window's S population, while the prose_long c=1 tok/s gain does not separate from S's own boot-to-boot range outside the pair. No multiple-testing correction is applied.

The rule and its baseline (the S boots interleaved with S1024, ARMS.md: 'the reference is the A boots of the same ABAB sequence') were fixed before the data. Re-baselining after seeing the result is the post-hoc choice the fixed rule exists to prevent, and the P5 decision applied the same principle in the other direction. The measured downside is small either way: +0.473 ms/step on L.A.I.L from the gather, greedy output unchanged, quality quick PASS. After this promotion the next window's A boots carry TOPK=1024 (ARMS-r3 s0), which will add same-config readings.

W-1's counted four_numbers ran about 9 min later in the boot than planned (the first capture was killed by a timeout wrapper, W-1/notes.txt DEVIATION), so W-1's four prose and prose_long cells came after extra traffic. The fresh L.A.I.L (lail10.txt, before any four_numbers) is unaffected, and the L.A.I.L gate cell alone already fails the revert (+0.431 against 0.81), so the SPARSE_MARKOV verdict does not depend on it.
If W were a promotion candidate it would also fail non-inferiority on pp_novel_8k (W minus S -15.15 against the larger spread 9.4). Recorded only; the revert already fails the speed gate.
